text:
{
  "background_info": "Student Name: Aryan Singh
School: Vidya Sagar School, Chennai
Grade: Grade 7 (Age: 13 years)
Date of IEP Meeting: 19 October 2026
Date Services Begin: 2 November 2026
Services Continue Through: 31 March 2027
Disability Classification: Hearing Impairment (Severe) under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act 2016
Dominant Language / Communication Mode: Indian Sign Language (ISL) and written English
Parent/Guardian Information: Mr. and Mrs. Singh (Contact: singh.family@email.com / +91-9876543210)
Medical Alerts: Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss; requires clear visual field and communication access at all times; no chronic physical medical conditions reported.",

  "academic_performance": "Present Level: Academic/Educational Achievement - Aryan Singh is currently functioning at grade level overall in his academic coursework, exhibiting notable strengths in Mathematics and Visual Arts where he demonstrates sophisticated numerical problem-solving and visual-spatial reasoning. However, Aryan is currently functioning below grade level in English language arts, specifically in reading comprehension and English vocabulary acquisition, due to the linguistic impact of auditory deprivation.
Present Level: Cognitive Ability - Aryan Singh is currently functioning at grade level in general cognitive processing, displaying advanced visual-spatial processing, non-verbal abstract reasoning, and systematic visual analytical skills.
Present Level: Language Ability - Aryan Singh is currently functioning above grade level in receptive and expressive Indian Sign Language (ISL) fluency; however, his English written language and vocabulary skills are currently below grade level, requiring structured bilingual-bimodal scaffolding (ISL-to-written English).
Present Level: Learning Style - Aryan is a dedicated visual learner who processes instructional content most effectively through Indian Sign Language (ISL), visual diagrams, graphic organizers, captioned media, and direct written texts.
Present Level: Rate of Progress - Aryan Singh is currently demonstrating a stable rate of progress in visual and computational subjects, with an accelerating trajectory when instruction is paired with consistent qualified ISL interpretation and visual-first curriculum materials.",

  "social_development": "Present Level: Relationships with Peers and Adults - Aryan Singh demonstrates positive, friendly social engagement and collaborates productively with peers and teachers whenever communication access is facilitated through Indian Sign Language (ISL) or written exchanges. He demonstrates high enthusiasm, cooperative teamwork in visual arts and mathematical group projects, and mutual respect in his classroom community.
Present Level: Self-Concept - Aryan displays a positive academic self-image and takes genuine pride in his artistic and mathematical accomplishments. He identifies strongly with the Deaf community and displays confidence when expressing ideas through ISL.
Present Level: Social Adjustment - Aryan participates actively in school routines when communication is barrier-free; however, he experiences occasional social isolation during unstructured conversational settings (such as lunch or recess) when sign-fluent peers or interpreters are not present.
Present Level: Behaviours That May Impede Learning - Aryan displays no disruptive, maladaptive, or non-compliant behaviors. In instances where interpreter access is disrupted or spoken instruction is presented without visual captions, Aryan may experience communication frustration or disengagement, highlighting the necessity of uninterrupted visual access.",

  "physical_development": "Present Level: Motor and Sensory Development - Aryan presents with normal gross and fine motor development, exhibiting exceptional fine motor coordination, precision, and visual-motor integration in drafting, sketching, and manual signing. Sensory development is characterized by severe bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment, which prevents the unassisted auditory reception of conversational speech.
Present Level: Health and Vitality - Aryan maintains robust physical health, high stamina, and age-appropriate physical endurance across the school day.
Present Level: Physical Skills and Limitations - Aryan exhibits full physical capability to engage in general physical education, sports, and practical laboratory activities, requiring only visual signals (e.g., visual flags, hand signals, or flash lights) rather than auditory cues (such as whistles) to participate fully and safely.",

  "management_needs": "Nature and Degree of Environmental Modifications: Aryan requires a front-row seating arrangement with an unobstructed, direct line of sight to the teacher, the Indian Sign Language interpreter, and the interactive whiteboard/screen. Lighting must be optimized to prevent glare and shadows that impede sign perception and lipreading. Environmental visual cues, such as flashing visual emergency alarms and visual timetable displays, are required across all learning spaces.
Human and Material Resources: Aryan requires significant human and material support, categorizing his management needs as significant. Human resources include a dedicated, qualified Indian Sign Language (ISL) interpreter for all academic instruction, a trained special educator for resource room language intervention, a designated peer note-taker, and school counselling support. Material resources include visual-first instructional media, advance lecture notes, captioned videos, and digital assistive technology devices. Redundancy planning must be maintained, ensuring trained backup interpreter coverage and automated speech-to-text live transcription software during any unscheduled interpreter absence.",

  "long_term_outcomes": "N/A — Student is below 14 years. Long-term adult outcomes and transition planning will be developed at age 14 per RPwD Act 2016 and NCTE Guidelines.",

  "annual_goals": "Annual Goal: By 31 March 2027, Aryan will independently plan, draft, and edit a three-paragraph structured written informational text in English scoring at least 80% on a standardized Grade 7 writing rubric.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Aryan will independently utilize visual graphic organizers to plan and structure written assignments across 4 out of 5 consecutive classroom writing tasks as measured by teacher-graded writing rubrics.
2. By the end of Term 2, Aryan will write cohesive multi-sentence paragraphs using at least 4 appropriate transitional phrases per text across 4 out of 5 work samples as measured by curriculum-based writing assessments.
3. By the end of Term 3, Aryan will edit written drafts to correct syntax, capitalization, and punctuation errors with 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive written assignments as measured by teacher-evaluated editing checklists.
Evaluation Procedures: Teacher-developed rubrics, written portfolio reviews, curriculum-based measurement.
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: By 31 March 2027, Aryan will demonstrate mastery of Grade 7 academic vocabulary by accurately identifying and defining 120 new subject-specific terms across Mathematics and Science using ISL and written English on 85% of quarterly trials.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Aryan will accurately match and define 40 Grade 7 mathematics and science terms using ISL-to-print bilingual vocabulary cards with 80% accuracy as measured by bi-weekly vocabulary quizzes.
2. By the end of Term 2, Aryan will expand subject-specific vocabulary in mathematics and science by 50 new terms using ISL-to-print flashcards with 85% accuracy as measured by bi-weekly vocabulary quizzes.
3. By the end of Term 3, Aryan will independently apply 30 advanced academic vocabulary terms in written explanatory sentences with 85% accuracy across 4 consecutive classroom evaluations as measured by teacher-graded criterion assessments.
Evaluation Procedures: Bi-weekly vocabulary quizzes, flashcard mastery tracking logs, criterion-referenced tests.
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: By 31 March 2027, Aryan will demonstrate independent reading comprehension of Grade 7 instructional texts by answering inferential and literal comprehension questions with 80% accuracy.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Aryan will identify main ideas and key supporting details from grade-level illustrated passages with 75% accuracy across 4 out of 5 trials as measured by reading comprehension check-ins.
2. By the end of Term 2, Aryan will answer direct and text-dependent inferential questions on grade-level texts with 80% accuracy across 4 out of 5 trials as measured by written comprehension rubrics.
3. By the end of Term 3, Aryan will summarize grade-level informational passages in writing using visual semantic maps with 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive assessments as measured by standardized reading probes.
Evaluation Procedures: Reading comprehension probes, semantic mapping rubrics, informal reading inventories.
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly",

  "special_education_services": "A. Special Education Programs and Related Services: Specialized academic instruction delivered by a trained special educator in a resource room setting for 5 sessions per week, 45 minutes per session, beginning 2 November 2026 and continuing through 31 March 2027, focusing on bilingual-bimodal English literacy and vocabulary development. Provision of counselling and social-emotional support by the school psychologist/counsellor for 1 session per week (40 minutes) beginning 2 November 2026 and continuing through 31 March 2027, pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30) regarding adequate facility of resource persons.

B. Extended School Year (ESY) Services: No. Aryan does not demonstrate substantial regression across academic breaks that would require extended school year programming.

C. Supplementary Aids and Modifications: 1. Full-time dedicated qualified Indian Sign Language (ISL) interpreter for all academic instruction, assemblies, co-curricular, and school activities pursuant to RPwD Act 2016 Section 16 and NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30) total communication approach. 2. Redundancy planning: In the event of an unplanned interpreter absence, an on-call certified backup interpreter will be assigned immediately; if temporarily unavailable, instructional content will be provided through live speech-to-text automated captioning and peer note-taking. 3. Visual-first instructional materials including captioned videos, visual graphic organizers, diagrams, and written step-by-step instructions pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30). 4. Dedicated note-taking support, including designated peer note-taker carbon copies and the provision of teacher lecture notes and presentation slides at least 24 hours in advance pursuant to reasonable accommodation mandates under RPwD Act 2016 Section 16 to allow Aryan to maintain visual focus on the interpreter.

D. Assistive Technology Devices and Services: 1. School-provided digital tablet equipped with offline and online Indian Sign Language (ISL) translation and dictionary applications, speech-to-text live transcription software for supplemental written support, and visual organizing tools pursuant to RPwD Act 2016 Section 16. 2. Noise-cancelling headphones for focused independent digital learning tasks to minimize auditory distractions.

E. Program Modifications and Supports for School Personnel: Bi-monthly collaborative consultation (30 minutes) between the general education teachers, the special educator, and the ISL interpreter. Professional development orientation for all Grade 7 faculty on Deaf culture, total communication methodology per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30), visual-first pedagogies, and best practices for working alongside an educational sign language interpreter.

F. Individual Testing Modifications: 1. Extended time of 50% (minimum 25% required) on all written class tests, quizzes, and summative assessments. 2. Separate, quiet testing environment with adequate lighting to minimize visual distractions and optimize focus. 3. Administration of instructions in Indian Sign Language (ISL) by the qualified interpreter to ensure full comprehension of test directions. 4. Use of assistive technology (digital tablet and speech-to-text software) during assessments as appropriate to disability.",

  "general_education_participation": "Aryan Singh will participate in the general education setting for approximately 85% of the instructional week, including all core academic subjects (Mathematics, Science, Social Sciences, Art, Physical Education, and non-academic school routines). He will be pulled out for specialized resource room instruction by the trained special educator for 5 periods per week (approximately 15% of instructional time) to address specific English language and vocabulary development.
Aryan will participate fully in all non-academic and extracurricular activities, including physical education, visual arts clubs, sports days, and school assemblies, supported by the dedicated ISL interpreter and visual signaling systems.
No second-language exemption is granted; Aryan will participate fully in the standard Grade 7 curriculum with appropriate bilingual (ISL and written text) instructional and assessment accommodations.",

  "participating_agencies": "N/A — Transition services not yet applicable. Will be identified at age 14.",

  "coordinated_activities": "1. Instruction: Specialized instruction in written English, reading comprehension, and subject-specific vocabulary by a trained special educator; total communication instructional delivery in general education via a dedicated Indian Sign Language interpreter.
2. Related Services: Indian Sign Language (ISL) interpretation services across all academic periods; school counselling and social-emotional guidance (1 session weekly) to foster self-advocacy and peer integration pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30).
3. Employment/Post-secondary Education: N/A — Student is 13 years of age.
4. Community Experience: N/A — Student is 13 years of age.
5. Activities of Daily Living: Integration of self-advocacy skills within classroom settings, including requesting communication clarifications and independently managing digital assistive technology.
6. Functional Vocational Assessment: N/A — Student is 13 years of age.",

  "graduation_info": "Aryan Singh is working toward the standard Secondary School Certificate (CBSE / State Board Certificate) at the completion of Grade 10, with an expected graduation completion year of 2030.
Board examination provisions will be requested under the reasonable accommodation provisions of the RPwD Act 2016, including compensatory extended time (minimum 25%), examination directions signed in Indian Sign Language, note-taker/scribe assistance if necessary, and testing in an accessible, quiet room. No second-language exemption is granted; Aryan will fulfill all standard curricular requirements with approved testing and communication accommodations.",

  "recommendations_summary": "Disability Classification: Hearing Impairment (Severe) under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act 2016 Schedule.
Recommended Placement: Inclusive general education Grade 7 classroom at Vidya Sagar School, Chennai, with dual resource room support (85% general education, 15% specialized resource room instruction) pursuant to RPwD Act 2016 Section 16.
Extended School Year (ESY) Services: ESY services are not recommended at this time.
Transportation Needs: Standard school transportation with visual stop notification monitors; no specialized medical transport needed.
Annual IEP Review Date: 19 October 2027.",

  "progress_reporting": "Manner and Frequency of Progress Reporting: Aryan Singh's progress toward all annual goals and short-term objectives will be reported to his parents on a quarterly schedule, matching the reporting frequency of his non-disabled peers.
Reporting Methods: Quarterly written IEP progress report cards containing objective data, curriculum-based measurement graphs, work sample portfolios, and rubrics measuring criterion achievement.
Criteria for Measuring Progress: Direct mastery of stated numerical criteria in short-term objectives (e.g., 80% accuracy across evaluated trials, rubric performance, and vocabulary quiz benchmarks).
Parent Meeting Schedule: Formal parent-teacher-special educator conferences will be conducted at the conclusion of each term (Quarterly: December 2026, March 2027, and during the annual review on 19 October 2027) with Indian Sign Language interpreter access available for all collaborative discussions."
}
